data.description: Fold the Organization settings design (prototype v1.15 iteration 3, rulings O1-O8) into the build, per sequence/org-settings-design.md — especially its 'Build implications' section, which is this ticket's scope list: organizations gains profile/default columns (default timezone, default theme, comms defaults, branding assets); POST /api/v1/org/invites gains role and event_id scope, exchange creates the membership with both, plus a short-code form of the one-time link; organizer removal extends the Amendment-19 in-transaction revocation to consume unexpired login links and revoke the member's created_by tokens in the same transaction; readTheme() falls back to the org default (per-user choice still wins); new person-record routes for remove-from-conference cascade (participations ended, reconcileTaskSet, event access revoked; published sessions untouched per O5a) and portal-access revocation; token move to /org/tokens is UI-only. Invite-only stands — no join-request queue. Contract fold (SPEC/USER_STORIES/AC mint) is part of this ticket, cold-start MRQ-105 style. Design contract: prototypes/pipeline-v1.1 org tabs (v1.15) + sequence/org-settings-design.md.
data.title: Organization settings fold: org surface, scoped invites, removal cascade, org defaults

MRQ-211 (PR #267) landed the named activity-recording seam you can call for the org admin lens.

src/lib/org-activity.ts:
  recordOrgActivity(db, entry)      — write one row now
  orgActivityStatement(db, entry)   — compose into your existing batch(); use this when the change itself is batched, so the record and the change share a transaction
  orgActor(auth)                    — actorKind/actorPersonId from the credential

entry = { orgId (required), eventId (optional — set it when the action is scoped to one conference; the lens resolves the name by join), actorKind, actorPersonId, action, entityType, entityId, before?, after?, now, requestId }.

Action names are constants in src/lib/activity-copy.ts — ORG_ACTIVITY_ACTIONS. Two are already defined and already read correctly in the lens; the writers are yours: org.defaults_changed (payload { changed: string[] }) and org.ownership_transferred (before { name }, after { name }).

Two things worth knowing:
- The org lens queries org_id, NOT a list of action names, so anything you write through the seam appears without touching the reader. An action the copy module has never met degrades to a readable sentence rather than a blank row (there is a test).
- If the subject of your action is a person (ownership transfer, a seat change), record entityType 'person' with their person_id — that is what puts it on their CRM feed (lens two) as well, with no extra work.

Also: migration 0019 makes audit_log.event_id nullable and adds org_id (a row must be scoped to at least one). If you touch audit_log, rebase onto that.

PR #263 / MRQ-207 adversarial review — PAUSED CONSOLIDATION

PATTERN: THE UNIT IS TRUE AND THE PRODUCT IS NOT. Findings 4, 6, 7, and 8 repeat the same defect: the test drives a helper or a hand-built API payload instead of the route the UI actually calls with the payload it actually sends. The assertion passes while the user-facing behavior is absent or inverted. Resume this ticket by rewriting those tests through the real path first; that change would have exposed all four.

1. FIXED IN LOCAL PAUSE COMMIT 2a04090f; reviewer verified the closing code path before the stop order — legacy invite still crossed tenants.
   Files: src/lib/auth/instance-claim.ts:76-83, 279-285; migrations/0020_org_invite_seats.sql:60-80.
   Inputs → wrong result before fix: create organizations A and B with A sorting first, then exchange an unspent pre-Amendment-21 org_invite intended for B whose invite_org_id is NULL. The exchange sent NULL through resolveOrganization(), selected A's first organization row, and created an owner membership in A.
   Why tests missed it: AC-296 minted only new post-migration invites, which already carried invite_org_id; it never inserted the legacy NULL row that bypassed the reported fix.
   Closing change: exchange now refuses unattributable NULL invite_org_id rows; migration 0020 backfills only the unambiguous one-organization case. Builder reports the regression was written failing-first and then passed.

2. FIXED IN LOCAL PAUSE COMMIT 2a04090f; reviewer verified the closing predicates before the stop order — invite list and revoke crossed tenants.
   File: src/routes/org-people.routes.ts:102-113, 230-247.
   Inputs → wrong result before fix: authenticate as an admin of organization A while organization B has a pending invite. GET /api/v1/org/invites returned B's invite metadata and ID; DELETE /api/v1/org/invites/{B-id} updated by ID and purpose alone, so A could spend B's invite.
   Why tests missed it: the invite tests exercised one authenticated organization at a time and never put another tenant's pending row beside it.
   Closing change: list is constrained by auth.orgId; revoke carries invite_org_id = auth.orgId on the UPDATE itself and returns the same 404 for foreign, spent, and absent rows. Builder reports the cross-tenant regression was written failing-first and then passed.

3. BUILDER REPORTS FIXED IN LOCAL PAUSE COMMIT 2a04090f; reviewer independently reproduced the pre-fix failure but did not re-review the in-flight fix after the operator's stop order — a scoped invite made its conference undeletable.
   Files: src/lib/auth/instance-claim.ts:168-175; src/lib/auth/magic-links.ts:101-107; src/lib/events/delete-event.ts:195-217, 296.
   Inputs → wrong result before fix: mint an ops invite scoped to event E. mintOrganizerInvite stored magic_links.event_id = NULL and invite_event_id = E. MRQ-204's cascade deleted magic links only through event_id, then DELETE events hit the new invite_event_id foreign key. Observed result against all migrations with node:sqlite: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed; E and the invite survived.
   Why tests missed it: MRQ-204 populated only magic_links.event_id; AC-296 minted the new scoped row but never deleted its event, so neither test covered the composition.
   Reported closing change: the cascade now also deletes by invite_event_id, with a failing-first regression asserting the event and invite disappear while the organization survives. Post-fix reviewer verification remains pending by operator order.

4. OPEN — the organization theme fallback is helper-true but product-false.
   Files: src/ui/shell/theme.ts:153-160; src/ui/org/OrgSettingsPage.tsx:104-117, 137; src/routes/org-settings.routes.ts:96-112.
   Inputs → wrong result: an owner sets organization default_theme to night; a newly invited reviewer or ops user opens Marquee in a fresh browser and has made no personal choice. marquee-org-default-theme is absent because the only production writer is the admin-only Organization tab after GET /api/v1/org/settings, which that user never traverses and may not access. Pre-paint/readTheme therefore returns day, not night.
   Why tests cannot catch it: AC-295 calls cacheOrgDefaultTheme() directly before calling readTheme(), manufacturing the storage state whose missing product wiring is the defect. No test drives the authenticated shell path for a non-admin user.

5. OPEN — remove-from-conference is not one transaction.
   File: src/routes/person-access.routes.ts:236-294.
   Inputs → wrong result: remove a person from event E while reconcileTaskSet throws after the first database batch (for example, a D1 write failure). Lines 240-274 have already committed participation deletion, task cancellation, membership removal, credential revocation, and audit; lines 281-293 then throw. The client receives 500 although removal already happened, and none of those writes can roll back.
   Why tests cannot catch it: AC-299 exercises only the success path; it never forces the post-batch reconciler to fail and checks no all-or-nothing outcome.

6. OPEN — the real organizer-removal UI under-revokes created_by Agent credentials.
   Files: src/ui/setup/OrganizersCard.tsx:109-123; src/routes/org-people.routes.ts:76-85, 363-376; src/routes/evaluation.routes.ts:1035-1038; src/lib/auth/auth-middleware.ts:44-54.
   Inputs → wrong result: organizer P creates an Agent evaluator seat and receives its bearer secret; an owner removes P through the actual OrganizersCard. The UI sends DELETE with no body, revoke_token_ids defaults to [], and no api_tokens UPDATE is added. That token is created_by P but acts_as the Agent; auth loads the surviving Agent membership, so P can keep using the known secret after removal.
   Why tests cannot catch it: arm three hand-builds a request containing revoke_token_ids and seeds only ordinary unbound tokens. It never sends the bodyless payload the UI sends and never makes a bearer request with a bound Agent token after removal.

7. OPEN — remove-from-conference over-revokes a different conference, and its survival test is vacuous for the risky case.
   Files: src/routes/person-access.routes.ts:240-260; src/lib/auth/access-revocation.ts:59-72; tests/integration/org-settings.AC-294-301.test.ts:534-640.
   Inputs → wrong result: the same org-level person has a live task or login link for event B, then is removed only from event A. removeFromConference calls revokeAccessStatements without an event, and consumeLinksStatement updates every live person-bound link by person_id, so B's link is consumed too.
   Why tests cannot catch it: AC-299 seeds no links. Its supposed elsewhere-survives case is a different person row in a different organization, not the same org person in a second conference. It also creates no agenda_items row; assertions at the former lines 597/625 inspect submissions.is_published only, so the test would remain green if the authoritative published agenda item were deleted or unpublished.

8. OPEN — an explicitly unchecked ordinary token does not keep working, inverting AC-298.
   Files: src/routes/org-people.routes.ts:363-376; src/lib/auth/auth-middleware.ts:54; src/lib/auth/scope-resolution.ts:112-116; tests/integration/org-settings.AC-294-301.test.ts:438-478.
   Inputs → wrong result: member P owns tokens A and B; the confirming owner names only A for revocation and intentionally leaves B unchecked to preserve a live integration. removeOrganizer deletes every non-speaker membership P holds. B remains revoked_at = NULL, but auth subsequently loads zero issuer memberships and tokenHasGrant rejects every bearer request with 403. The integration the checkbox promised to preserve is down.
   Why tests cannot catch it: arm three asserts only that B.revoked_at is NULL. It never makes the required positive-control bearer request with B after removal, so a dead token is reported as kept-working.

Pause boundary: findings 1 and 2 were code-path verified locally before the stop order; finding 3 is builder-reported fixed with the pre-fix failure independently reproduced; findings 4-8 remain open. No exact pushed-head approval is claimed.

PAUSED by operator ruling at head 52062048 (PR #263, branch mrq-207-org-settings-fold, pushed). Full state is in the PR body; this comment duplicates it because a PR body can be lost to a force-push.

FIXED, each failing-test-first with the failure observed before the fix:
(1) CROSS-TENANT — instance-claim.ts: an org_invite with NULL invite_org_id reached resolveOrganization(), which returns the OLDEST organization row, so an Org B invite minted a membership in Org A. Now refused outright; migration 0020 backfills only the unambiguous single-organization case. Test 'an unattributable legacy invite is refused rather than minted into whichever organization sorts first' — exchanged 200 into Org A before, 401 with zero rows after.
(2) CROSS-TENANT — org-people.routes.ts: any org admin could enumerate AND revoke every other tenant's pending invites. Both scoped to auth.orgId with the predicate ON THE UPDATE (a check-then-act is still wrong when the write is unscoped); uniform 404 so a refusal cannot confirm another tenant's invite exists. Test 'one organization's admin can neither see nor revoke another's pending invites'.
(3) FUNCTIONAL BLOCK — a live conference-scoped invite made its conference undeletable (FK constraint). MRQ-204's cascade deletes magic_links by event_id only; a scoped invite points at the event via invite_event_id. Cascade extended. NOT fixed by populating event_id too — two columns meaning one thing is how the next cascade bug gets written. Test reproduced the 500 before, passes after.
(6) LIVE CREDENTIAL — OrganizersCard sends DELETE with NO BODY and revoke_token_ids defaulted to [], so every ordinary removal revoked nothing and a removed organizer kept a working bearer secret. Agent-evaluator tokens make this worse: created_by = the human, acts_as_person_id = the seat, and authority resolves through the SEAT's membership, which survives removal. Inverted to ruling O3's actual wording — revoke is the default, keep_token_ids is the explicit exception. Test drives the real no-body request and then ATTEMPTS THE BEARER: 200 before, 401 after.

OPEN — do not merge until closed. File:line and reproduction in the PR body, not summarised:
(4) AC-295 is unit-true, not product-true: the org default theme reaches only org admins, because the only writer of the storage key is behind the admin-only GET /api/v1/org/settings. A newly invited reviewer or ops user never gets it. PARTIAL: GET /api/v1/auth/me now returns org_default_theme; the shell does not consume it yet.
(5) AC-299 is not atomic: reconcileTaskSet runs after the DB.batch commits, so a throw reports 500 for a removal that already happened. Ruled shape: keep the call, make the tail truthful rather than fatal, and assert the throw path.
(7) CROSS-CONFERENCE BLEED: remove-from-conference consumes EVERY person-bound link by person_id with no event predicate, so removing someone from Event A kills their Event B link — the CLAUDE.md invariant that cannot be undone. PARTIAL: consumeLinksStatement takes an optional eventId and revokeConferenceAccessStatements exists with the reasoning written out; its caller is NOT switched yet, so the helper is currently unused.
(8) Two test weaknesses that hide (7) and ruling O5a: the 'elsewhere survives' case uses a different person in a different ORG rather than the same org person at a second conference; and no agenda_items row is seeded, so the published-session assertion only checks submissions.is_published when O5a is about the published session.

THE PATTERN, the most useful thing this PR produced: findings 4, 6, 7 and 8 are all THE UNIT IS TRUE AND THE PRODUCT IS NOT — each test drove the helper rather than the path a real user takes. Before adding a test here, ask whether it goes through the route the UI actually calls with the payload the UI actually sends.

CROSS-PR CONSTRAINTS for whoever resumes: apply-migrations.ts keeps BOTH 0017 and 0018 imports in numeric order (a dropped import is a migration that silently never applies). The magic_links columns MUST stay in 0020, never 0017 — 0018 rebuilds that table and would copy them away with no error. Amendment 21 sits before Amendment 22, final marker AC-308.
